subject: Data Structures

intro.en: A binary search tree keeps data sorted in a tree shape so that searching, inserting and deleting can be fast.
intro.ru: Binary search tree data ko tree ki shakal mein tarteeb se rakhta hai taake search, insert aur delete tez ho sakein.

definition.en: A binary search tree (BST) is a binary tree in which every key in a node's left subtree is smaller than the node's key and every key in its right subtree is larger.
definition.ru: Binary search tree (BST) aisa binary tree hai jis mein har node ke left subtree ki har key us node ki key se chhoti aur right subtree ki har key bari hoti hai.

explanation.en: To search, compare the key with the root and go left if it is smaller or right if it is larger, repeating until the key is found or a null child is reached. Insertion follows the same path and adds the new key as a leaf. Deleting a node with two children replaces it with its in-order successor (the smallest key in its right subtree). All of these take O(h) time where h is the height: O(log n) for a balanced tree but O(n) for a skewed tree (e.g. inserting sorted data). Self-balancing trees such as AVL and red-black trees keep h = O(log n). An in-order traversal (left, node, right) visits the keys in sorted order.
explanation.ru: Search ke liye key ko root se milayein: chhoti ho to left, bari ho to right jayein, aur yahi dohrayein jab tak key mil na jaye ya khali child aa jaye. Insertion isi raste par chal kar nayi key ko leaf ke taur par lagati hai. Do children wali node delete karne ke liye use in-order successor (right subtree ki sab se chhoti key) se badla jata hai. Yeh sab O(h) waqt lete hain jahan h height hai: balanced tree mein O(log n) lekin skewed tree (maslan sorted data insert karna) mein O(n). AVL aur red-black jaise self-balancing trees h = O(log n) rakhte hain. In-order traversal (left, node, right) keys ko tarteeb se dikhata hai.

example.en: Insert 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80. Root 50; 30 goes left; 70 right; 20 left of 30; 40 right of 30; 60 left of 70; 80 right of 70. Searching 60: 60 > 50 go right to 70, 60 < 70 go left, found in 3 comparisons. In-order traversal: 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80.
example.ru: 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80 insert karein. Root 50; 30 left; 70 right; 20, 30 ke left; 40, 30 ke right; 60, 70 ke left; 80, 70 ke right. 60 search: 60 > 50 to right 70 par, 60 < 70 to left, 3 muqablon mein mil gaya. In-order traversal: 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80.

subject: Operating Systems

intro.en: Deadlock is a classic operating-system problem in which programs wait for each other forever, so none of them can continue.
intro.ru: Deadlock operating system ka classic masla hai jis mein programs hamesha ek doosre ka intezar karte rehte hain aur koi aage nahi barh pata.

definition.en: A deadlock is a state in which each process in a set holds at least one resource and waits for a resource held by another process in the same set, so none of them can proceed.
definition.ru: Deadlock aisi halat hai jis mein ek group ka har process kam az kam ek resource pakre hota hai aur usi group ke kisi doosre process ke resource ka intezar karta hai, is liye koi bhi aage nahi barh sakta.

explanation.en: A deadlock can only happen when four (Coffman) conditions hold at the same time: mutual exclusion (a resource can be used by one process at a time), hold and wait (a process holds resources while waiting for more), no preemption (resources cannot be taken away), and circular wait (a cycle of processes each waiting for the next). Handling strategies: prevention breaks one condition (e.g. request all resources at once, or order resources and always request them in that order); avoidance grants requests only if the system stays in a safe state (Banker's algorithm); detection builds a wait-for / resource-allocation graph and looks for a cycle, then recovers by terminating a process or preempting resources; or the system ignores the problem (the 'ostrich' approach used by many desktop OSs).
explanation.ru: Deadlock sirf tab hota hai jab chaar (Coffman) conditions ek saath poori hon: mutual exclusion (resource ek waqt mein ek process istemal kare), hold and wait (process resources pakre hue mazeed ka intezar kare), no preemption (resources cheene nahi ja sakte), aur circular wait (processes ka daira jis mein har ek agle ka intezar kare). Hal ke tareeqe: prevention ek condition tor deta hai (maslan saare resources ek saath maangna, ya resources ko tarteeb de kar hamesha usi tarteeb mein maangna); avoidance sirf tab request deta hai jab system safe state mein rahe (Banker's algorithm); detection wait-for / resource-allocation graph bana kar cycle dhoondta hai, phir process khatam kar ke ya resources cheen kar recover karta hai; ya system masle ko nazar andaz karta hai ('ostrich' tareeqa, kai desktop OS yahi karte hain).

example.en: Process P1 holds the printer and requests the scanner. Process P2 holds the scanner and requests the printer. Both wait forever: mutual exclusion (one user per device), hold and wait (each holds one), no preemption (the OS will not take the printer away), circular wait (P1 -> P2 -> P1). If both processes always request the printer before the scanner (resource ordering), circular wait is impossible and the deadlock cannot occur.
example.ru: Process P1 printer pakre hue scanner maangta hai. Process P2 scanner pakre hue printer maangta hai. Dono hamesha intezar karte rehte hain: mutual exclusion (ek device ka ek user), hold and wait (har ek ne ek pakra hai), no preemption (OS printer nahi cheenta), circular wait (P1 -> P2 -> P1). Agar dono hamesha pehle printer phir scanner maangein (resource ordering), to circular wait mumkin nahi aur deadlock nahi hoga.

subject: Computer Networks
search_query: tcp three way handshake syn ack

intro.en: Before TCP sends any data, the two computers agree to talk and synchronise their sequence numbers. This short exchange is the three-way handshake.
intro.ru: TCP data bhejne se pehle dono computers baat karne par ittefaq karte hain aur apne sequence numbers milate hain. Yeh chhota sa tabadla three-way handshake hai.

definition.en: The TCP three-way handshake establishes a connection with three segments: the client sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, and the client answers ACK.
definition.ru: TCP three-way handshake teen segments se connection banata hai: client SYN bhejta hai, server SYN-ACK se jawab deta hai, aur client ACK bhejta hai.

explanation.en: 1) The client sends a segment with the SYN flag and a random initial sequence number x. 2) The server replies with SYN and ACK flags, its own initial sequence number y and acknowledgement number x + 1 (meaning 'I received your SYN'). 3) The client sends ACK with acknowledgement number y + 1. Now both sides know each other's starting sequence numbers and the connection is ESTABLISHED. Three messages are the minimum that confirms both directions work. Random initial sequence numbers protect against old duplicate segments and spoofing. A SYN flood attack sends many SYNs without completing step 3, filling the server's half-open connection queue. Closing uses FIN and ACK segments from both sides (a four-way exchange).
explanation.ru: 1) Client SYN flag aur random shuruati sequence number x ke saath segment bhejta hai. 2) Server SYN aur ACK flags, apne shuruati sequence number y aur acknowledgement number x + 1 ke saath jawab deta hai (matlab 'tumhara SYN mil gaya'). 3) Client acknowledgement number y + 1 ke saath ACK bhejta hai. Ab dono ko ek doosre ke shuruati sequence numbers maloom hain aur connection ESTABLISHED hai. Teen messages kam se kam hain jo dono simton ka kaam karna tasdeeq karte hain. Random shuruati sequence numbers purane duplicate segments aur spoofing se bachate hain. SYN flood attack bohat se SYN bhejta hai lekin step 3 poora nahi karta, jis se server ki adhoore connections wali queue bhar jati hai. Band karne ke liye dono taraf se FIN aur ACK segments jate hain (chaar hisson wala tabadla).

example.en: Client initial sequence number = 1000, server initial sequence number = 5000. 1) Client -> Server: SYN, seq = 1000. 2) Server -> Client: SYN-ACK, seq = 5000, ack = 1001. 3) Client -> Server: ACK, seq = 1001, ack = 5001. The first data byte from the client will have sequence number 1001.
example.ru: Client ka shuruati sequence number = 1000, server ka = 5000. 1) Client -> Server: SYN, seq = 1000. 2) Server -> Client: SYN-ACK, seq = 5000, ack = 1001. 3) Client -> Server: ACK, seq = 1001, ack = 5001. Client ke pehle data byte ka sequence number 1001 hoga.

subject: Databases

intro.en: Normalization is how database designers organise tables so that the same fact is not stored in many places, which avoids inconsistent data.
intro.ru: Normalization ke zariye database designers tables ko aise tarteeb dete hain ke ek hi baat kai jagah save na ho, taake data be-rabt (inconsistent) na ho.

definition.en: Normalization is the process of decomposing relational tables, guided by functional dependencies, to reduce redundancy and avoid insertion, update and deletion anomalies.
definition.ru: Normalization functional dependencies ki rehnumai mein relational tables ko chhote tables mein todne ka amal hai, taake redundancy kam ho aur insertion, update aur deletion anomalies se bacha ja sake.

explanation.en: A functional dependency A -> B means the value of A determines the value of B. First normal form (1NF): every column holds a single atomic value (no lists). Second normal form (2NF): 1NF and no non-key column depends on only part of a composite primary key (no partial dependency). Third normal form (3NF): 2NF and no non-key column depends on another non-key column (no transitive dependency). Boyce-Codd normal form (BCNF) is stricter: the left side of every non-trivial functional dependency must be a candidate key. The smaller tables are linked again with foreign keys. Over-normalising can slow reads because queries need many joins, so some systems denormalise on purpose.
explanation.ru: Functional dependency A -> B ka matlab hai A ki value B ki value tay karti hai. First normal form (1NF): har column mein ek hi atomic value (lists nahi). Second normal form (2NF): 1NF aur koi non-key column composite primary key ke sirf ek hisse par munhasir na ho (partial dependency nahi). Third normal form (3NF): 2NF aur koi non-key column doosre non-key column par munhasir na ho (transitive dependency nahi). Boyce-Codd normal form (BCNF) zyada sakht hai: har non-trivial functional dependency ka baayan hissa candidate key ho. Chhote tables foreign keys se dobara jore jate hain. Zyada normalisation reads ko dheema kar sakti hai kyunki queries ko bohat se joins chahiye, is liye kuch systems jaan boojh kar denormalise karte hain.

example.en: Table Enrollment(student_id, course_id, student_name, course_title, instructor, instructor_office) with key (student_id, course_id). student_name depends only on student_id and course_title only on course_id: partial dependencies, so it is not 2NF. Split into Student(student_id, student_name), Course(course_id, course_title, instructor, instructor_office) and Enrollment(student_id, course_id). In Course, instructor_office depends on instructor (a non-key column): a transitive dependency, so split again into Course(course_id, course_title, instructor) and Instructor(instructor, instructor_office) to reach 3NF.
example.ru: Table Enrollment(student_id, course_id, student_name, course_title, instructor, instructor_office), key (student_id, course_id). student_name sirf student_id par aur course_title sirf course_id par munhasir hai: partial dependencies, yaani 2NF nahi. Todein: Student(student_id, student_name), Course(course_id, course_title, instructor, instructor_office) aur Enrollment(student_id, course_id). Course mein instructor_office instructor (non-key) par munhasir hai: transitive dependency, is liye 3NF ke liye mazeed todein: Course(course_id, course_title, instructor) aur Instructor(instructor, instructor_office).
